clause: Raster-domain cross-cutting obligations + dedup-completeness conformance harness [STU-RAS-001,STU-RAS-002,STU-RAS-003,STU-RAS-004,STU-RAS-005,STU-RAS-047,STU-RAS-048]

scope.summary: Build the raster-domain conformance harness that mechanically enforces the 14.4 cross-cutting obligations once for every raster command: each command that creates/changes/removes an operator-visible surface has (a) a GUI control, (b) a schemars inputSchema-carrying typed command, (c) Argus receipts + snapshot path, (d) a UserManual entry; plus quiet-law compliance, sandbox->validation->PromotionGate lifecycle on model mutations, StudioRasterTile-only pixel storage (no full-frame buffers), and per-op StudioHistoryEntry reversibility. Include a dedup-completeness check asserting every 14.4 clause/table-row maps to at least one registered raster command and no source-suite product name leaks as a Studio tool/panel/command name.
acceptance_criteria: conformance harness enforces GUI+command+Argus+manual on every raster command
proof_targets: fail-closed model-mutation negative test + per-command obligation coverage check
expected_tests: live: model-authored raster mutation is refused a direct authority write and forced through sandbox->validation->PromotionGate (fails closed)
test: every registered raster command_id has GUI target + inputSchema + Argus receipt + manual entry; no source-suite product name appears as a Studio command/panel name

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Headless/backend MT: no operator-visible surface changed.

user_manual_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Non-product-behavior or internal-scaffold MT; UserManual updated by the consuming feature MT.

risk_if_missed: Raster features ship without the uniform GUI/command/Argus/manual + promotion guarantees; obligations silently omitted per feature.

risks: Scaffold-only claim without runtime proof (Spec-Realism Gate).
Domain MT forking a canonical primitive instead of referencing 14.23.
SQLite creep on a studio_* write path.
minimum_controls: At least one proof command exercises executable runtime or a Handshake-managed resource boundary.
Reference canonical primitives (14.23); no shadow primitives.
